C) Your Lordships may be pleased to issue writ of mandamus or any other writ order,
direction, declaring the acquisition of the land that was acquired way back in the year 1939 and the award that was made in 1959 was illegal, bad and in violation of the fundamental rights guaranteed under the constitution of India, in the interest of justice.

D) Your Lordships may be pleased to grant such other and further relief that may be deemed fit and proper in the interest of justice."
4.

The submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the entire acquisition proceedings which were conducted in the year 1939 though culminated with the making of the award on 29.10.1959, is to be declared as lapsed, inasmuch as, the land in question has not been utilized for the purposes for which it was acquired, is found to be wholly misconceived.

There is nothing on record which would indicate that the land in question has remained in the possession of the original land holders during whose lifetime, acquisition proceedings were brought to its logical end.

It may further be noted that as per the statement in the writ petition, NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9226/2018 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined the land in question belonged to one Chunilal Girjashankar Vyas, who had expired but his date of death is not indicated therein.
It is stated in paragraph no. 2 of the writ petition that the heirs of Chunilal Girjashankar Vyas namely Jadav Chunilal Vyas had expired in the year 1960.
It, thus, seems that the then owner of the land-in-question had died after the land acquisition proceedings were culminated with the making of the award in the year 1959.

It, therefore, does not lie in the mouth of the petitioner who was not even born when the land in question was acquired, to say anything with regard to the payment of the compensation to the then land holders.

All grounds taken in the writ petition to assail the acquisition with the assertion that no notice for payment of compensation had ever been served to the petitioner or his predecessor, is to be rejected outrightly being neither here not there.
The submission that the land in question has been acquired illegally, cannot be examined at the instance of the petitioner after a period of 59 years.
5. None of the prayers made in the writ petition can be entertained.

sentences.text: Moreover, Mr. Anuj Trivedi, learned advocate for the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9226/2018 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined respondent - Corporation has made a submission during the course of the arguments to the effect that the land acquisition award was passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer on 29.10.1959 and the respondent - Corporation had deposited the compensation on 23.11.1959 pursuant to the said award.

The then owner of the land in question had challenged the award before the competent Civil Court in Compensation case No. 18 of 1961 filed on 26.10.1964, wherein the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer was upheld.
7. A First Appeal No. 68 of 1965 was filed by the then owner, which had been partly allowed by this Court awarding some additional amount of compensation.
Pursuant thereto, the Special Land Acquisition Officer addressed a letter dated 20.09.1971 to the respondent - Corporation to deposit the additional amount, which was duly deposited on 13.10.1971.

The submission, thus, is that the present petition has been filed with malafide intention by suppression of the material facts and the assertions and allegations made in the writ petition are absolutely false.

8. Considering the above, noticing that as per the own case of the petitioner, the land acquisition proceedings had been NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9226/2018 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined brought to its logical end in the year 1959, the petitioner who was born sometime in the year 1963 cannot be permitted to raise any challenge, either to the acquisition proceedings or any issue relating to the payment of compensation to the then land holders.
9.
The writ petition is accordingly, dismissed as wholly misconceived.
No order as to costs.
